key_insight: Integrating tactile sensing with video-based action models lets agents infer contact-rich dynamics that are partially or ambiguously observable from vision alone, enabling fine-grained force modulation and more reliable contact transitions.
problem_solved: Video-Action Models (VAMs) struggle in contact-rich physical interactions because critical interaction states (force, slip, micro-contact) are only partially observable from vision, limiting precise control and safe manipulation.
method: Extend VAMs to Video-Tactile-Action Models (VTAMs) by fusing visual streams with tactile signals to learn joint spatiotemporal dynamics.
Use a multimodal encoder + temporal dynamics predictor that produces temporally consistent, touch-aware action predictions for force modulation and contact transitions.
Train end-to-end on sequences that include contact events so the model internalizes tactile-visual correlations and produces control-relevant outputs (actions/commands).
impact: VTAMs make embodied agents and robots more capable and robust in contact-rich manipulation tasks by adding a complementary sensing modality, reducing failure modes from partial observability and improving safety and finesse in real-world interactions.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: camera + tactile sensor inputs → multimodal encoder → temporal dynamics module → action decoder
Side-by-side timeline: VAM (vision-only) vs VTAM (vision + touch) showing improved detection of contact events and smoother force profiles
Example sequence visuals: frames showing a robotic hand approaching, contacting, and manipulating an object with overlaid tactile signal plots
Bar/line chart summarizing qualitative gains (e.g., fewer contact failures, improved force stability) on representative contact-rich tasks
paper_title: VTAM: Video-Tactile-Action Models for Complex Physical Interaction Beyond VLAs
paper_authors: Haoran Yuan, Weigang Yi, Zhenyu Zhang, Wendi Chen, Yuchen Mo
